Planarity, faces, genus, duals and crossings, tested against graphs whose
answers have been known for a century, because this is the notebook where a
wrong result is hardest to notice.

Planarity is right 13 times out of 13, including on two different drawings of
the same graph, so the operator reads the graph and not the picture. Euler's
identity holds on every connected planar case, with the outer face counted, and
the crossing counts match an independent combinatorial oracle.

What sits on top of that does not hold. The genus routine returns 0 for K₃,₃ and
for the Petersen graph, both established as non-planar by the same function
moments earlier, because its bound ignores the planarity result it has just
computed. Every non-planar graph is reported as containing an "unknown
subdivision", since the call that would identify it goes to a NetworkX function
that does not exist.
